title: skopeo-experimental-proxy: design goals? is writing something that's aimed for?
body:
Hey, I've been using `containers_image_proxy` and it's been great, and I know behind the scenes it uses `skopeo`'s experimental-image-proxy. However, the one gap I've been seeing when I use it is that I can't do any of skopeo's operations that aren't just *reading*. Some of my most common uses of skopeo as a CLI tool are for `copy` and sometimes `delete`. 

I was wondering if that was an intentional design choice in that it's supposed to be a nice tool to *read* images, or if it's just a current hole in the impl. I would be happy to PR something if it's the latter. I'm assuming if it's the former the desired path for such would be something like the podman API? Or is that just kind of out of scope?

comments.body:
The proxy features are rather driven by the primary user, bootc + friends. It’s never been a design goal to expose _everything_; after all, software developers can “just” write their own Go software that calls c/image.

I’d also say that the write paths are _significantly_ more complex, especially when trying to do things optimally (e.g. not copy large layers that already exist at the destination).

Realistically, with AI submissions PR review is by far the biggest bottleneck in the project and as is, proxy writes is not a feature we can spend much time on for the next few months _at least_.

Write support just came up in https://github.com/composefs/composefs-rs/pull/436#issuecomment-6659192085 xref https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/pull/651 which touches on this.

I think it'd make sense to generalize the varlink API.

> after all, software developers can “just” write their own Go software that calls c/image.

It's more complicated than that as you know, there's an enormous cost (binary size, logistics) to having more Go binaries using container-libs, especically when the *rest* of the software is not Go.

> Realistically, with AI submissions PR review is by far the biggest bottleneck in the project and as is, proxy writes is not a feature we can spend much time on for the next few months at least.

I completely agree that's a key problem, but I think it's still useful to ensure that projects have a roadmap for where they want to go, and this is a good example of that.

I am still hopeful we can get agreement on that varlink-based API using splitdirfdstream as a way to access image content more natively.

> Some of my most common uses of skopeo as a CLI tool are for copy and sometimes delete.

I know I've cross-referenced these a few times but are you mainly interested in things like a progress API? That's https://github.com/containers/skopeo/issues/658

My case was, at the moment, was writing a tool that is using buildah in the back but is currently written in Rust. We could "just" rewrite it in Go like specified or have our own wrapper thing but I figured I'd ask upstream since the case of doing 'copy' seemed fairly similar to the rest of the stuff in terms of I would've just been looking for ImageReference to ImageReference like skopeo takes. If it's worth anything, I don't want to use AI to write any of this to begin with, but I imagine that doesn't matter much for the overlying issue of number of PRs and amount of code for the most part at least.
